Done. Summary of what I saved:

The miss (0.3723 vs gold 0.3719, Δ=0.0004) was a near-miss, not a method failure — the Pearson formula was right, but one of the ~8 extracted cell values was slightly off. Generalizable lessons recorded into the existing `r-squared-between-two-series.md` reference and its SKILL.md pointer:

1. New table location: nonbanking-firms' foreign-currency-positions table (Capital Movements series, 1970s-80s bulletins) — currencies are columns, quarterly month-ends are rows, values in millions of the foreign unit.

2. Pearson-r variant vs R²: this question asks for r itself (not squared), and r can be negative — distinct from the FFO-1 R² question already in the ref.

3. The reusable precision rule: with only ~4 data points, an r that's off only at the 4th decimal means exactly ONE mis-extracted cell. Fix = never pre-round intermediates (feed raw integer millions to np.corrcoef, round only the final r), re-read all 2N cells digit-by-digit, verify quarter/year rows (quarterly tables repeat month names every year), and confirm you didn't swap an adjacent currency column.

No memory change needed — this is covered by the existing near-miss note ("digits match gold but small final-decimal miss = extraction error") and is now concretely actionable in the skill.
